head: 339dd9f0a5c59fed2e40b550516bd50a2bf50ceb
summary:
HF-008 is fixed as the design said. Commit 339dd9f deletes only the 30-line '# settled by SL-043' block from .taad/fitness.yaml, which held the three settled entries and their comment. The twinned entries at fitness.yaml:191-219 are strict supersets of what was deleted. They use the same files globs and the same patterns: the added (?m) changes nothing because none of these patterns has a ^ or $ anchor. They also set including_comments: true, so they match comments as well as code. The App no-wait entry at :206-212 is untouched. The deleted 'The App may wait on it' reason now appears nowhere in the tree. Nothing else in the tree referred to the deleted entries. I checked eng/rules-harness plants.json and divergences.json, tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1, which find the first '# settled by' marker and that marker is still SL-023, the Core.Tests files that read fitness.yaml, and docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:313-315. The docs table already describes the twinned App+Core scope. Checks I ran myself: Fitness op=check on the worktree reported 61 rules and 'Every declared rule holds'. eng/rules-parity.ps1 printed 'AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 46 settled entries not compared', exit 0. The xUnit tests that read fitness.yaml, RuleCopiesAgreeTests and ArchitectureRulesTests, passed 12 of 12. The xUnit authority at ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:125-155 still enforces all three rules, and the App scope is at :141. The design listed no cases, so there is no case matrix to walk. The slice index shows one build attempt and no loop. The builder's open items are follow-ups and do not block this slice: no test pins the duplicate-report shape, and no guard refuses a settled entry that duplicates a twinned one. I did not re-run the full 400-test suite. It is the builder's claim, and a yaml-only change can reach the suite only through the tests I did run.

Second round: The second round found nothing new. The diff adds no parser, matcher, regex or reader. It only deletes 30 lines of .taad/fitness.yaml, so no input format is widened and no new boundary is created. I walked every reader of the file for what the deletion could break. RuleCases.ps1:211-229 and rules-parity.ps1 part the file at the first '# settled by' marker, which is still SL-023. SettledCountProbe.ps1:104 counts entries under every marker, and nothing keys on the SL-043 marker in particular. The rules-harness plants.json and divergences.json have no rows for the deleted names. The yaml still parses: Fitness checked 61 rules, rules-parity printed AGREE with 46 settled, and the 12 xUnit tests that read the yaml passed. I also looked at the one writer outside this repo, the engine's append in taad3/design.py:1055-1085. It appends only rule names it has not seen, so if SL-043's design were ever landed again the three deleted names would be appended again. SL-043 is merged and does not re-run design, so this is not a defect of this slice. I did not file it.

obligations.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml: git diff f8b98c48d..HEAD shows only the deletion of the '# settled by SL-043' block (the three entries 'the classifier does not list link tags…', 'nothing in Core waits on the volume figure' and 'the volume read cannot hold a scan's memory', plus their 3-line comment). The twinned supersets remain at :191-219, and NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App) at :206-212 is unchanged. A grep for 'App may wait', 'outside this glob' and the three deleted names outside .taad/slices finds only docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:313, which describes the twinned or xUnit rule. Fitness check: 61 rules, all hold. rules-parity: AGREE, 46 settled.

drift: None. The build did what the design's fix said and nothing else: it deleted the three settled SL-043 entries and their explanatory comment. It declared that it added no test, and that is consistent with a design that has no cases.
None. The build is the design's fix and nothing more.
